proposals.before: New policies multiplied and officials strained every nerve for gain, while the sage-kings' counsel—to swell the population, lighten consumption, and husband resources in haste—was left unheeded.
proposals.after: New policies multiplied and officials strained every nerve for gain, while the sage-kings' counsel—to increase the multitude and lessen consumption, to produce with urgency and spend with ease—was left unheeded.
proposals.reason: 为疾用舒 means produce urgently and spend leisurely/with ease; 'husband resources in haste' reverses and conflates the classical pair.

proposals.before: New policies proliferated, and they strove unceasingly to seek profit; yet regarding the way of the ancient sage-kings—to increase the people and reduce consumption, and to use resources sparingly in times of urgency—they were ignorant and did not discuss it.
proposals.after: New policies proliferated, and they strove unceasingly to seek profit; yet regarding the way of the ancient sage-kings—to increase the people and reduce consumption, and to produce with urgency while spending with ease—they were ignorant and did not discuss it.
proposals.reason: 为疾用舒 is produce-with-urgency and use-with-ease, not 'use resources sparingly in times of urgency'.

decisions.reason: In s0013, 生眾食寡、為疾用舒 is the classical fiscal pair: increase producers/multitude and lessen consumption, then produce with urgency and spend with ease. The prior idiomatic 'husband resources in haste' conflates and reverses 為疾用舒; the proposed replacement restores that sense without inventing content.

The same focus phrase 為疾用舒 pairs urgent production (為疾) with leisurely spending (用舒). The prior literal 'use resources sparingly in times of urgency' misreads that pair; the proposed 'produce with urgency while spending with ease' matches the Chinese.
